name: Germany
genZNote: Germany rebuilt itself from a divided, war-shattered nation into Europe's biggest economy in a few decades — the 'Wirtschaftswunder' (economic miracle) is basically the textbook case study for how fast a country can recover with the right institutions.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in Central Europe, bordered by nine countries — more neighbours than any other European nation — including France, Poland, and the Netherlands.
Terrain ranges from flat northern plains along the North and Baltic Seas to the Alps in the south, with the Rhine and Danube as major rivers.
Historically divided into East and West Germany from 1949 until reunification in 1990 following the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: German is the official language; the country has a globally influential tradition in philosophy, classical music (Beethoven, Bach), and literature (Goethe).
Strong regional cultural identities persist across its 16 federal states (Länder), each with distinct traditions and dialects.
A deep national reckoning with its 20th-century history, particularly the Holocaust and Nazi era, strongly shapes contemporary civic culture and education.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal parliamentary republic; the Chancellor is head of government (elected by the Bundestag), while the President serves a largely ceremonial head-of-state role.
Composed of 16 federal states (Länder), each with significant autonomous powers, reflecting a strong tradition of federalism.
Reunified in 1990 after nearly 45 years of Cold War division between democratic West Germany and communist East Germany.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A global leader in engineering, automotive technology (Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz), and industrial manufacturing ('Mittelstand' small-and-medium enterprises).
Home to world-renowned research institutions (Max Planck Society, Fraunhofer Institutes) and numerous Nobel laureates across the sciences.
A major global pharmaceutical and biotechnology hub; BioNTech's mRNA COVID-19 vaccine (developed with Pfizer) was a landmark recent contribution.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Europe's largest economy and a founding member of the European Union, playing a central leadership role in EU policy.
A NATO member and key transatlantic security partner, though historically cautious about military deployments given its 20th-century history.
A major driver of the Eurozone's monetary and economic policy given the scale of its economy.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Germany share a 'Strategic Partnership', with Germany being one of India's largest European trade partners and sources of foreign investment.
Strong cooperation in renewable energy, skilled labour migration, vocational training, and advanced manufacturing/engineering technology transfer.
Germany has been a long-standing partner in India's industrial and infrastructure development since the early decades after Indian independence.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: The largest economy in Europe and a global manufacturing and export powerhouse, especially in automobiles, machinery, and chemicals.
Home to globally leading companies including Volkswagen, Siemens, BASF, and SAP.
A strong exporter nation with a persistent trade surplus, underpinned by high-value engineering and industrial goods.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Post-WWII reunification (1990) and its post-war economic transformation ('Wirtschaftswunder').
World-leading automotive and precision engineering industries.
Being the largest and most influential economy within the European Union.
A deep and reflective public reckoning with its Nazi-era history.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Germany is Europe's largest economy and a federal parliamentary republic, reunified in 1990 after Cold War division, and a founding EU member state.
keyFacts: Federal parliamentary republic; Chancellor is head of government, President is ceremonial head of state.
Reunified in 1990 after ~45 years of division between West and East Germany.
Europe's largest economy; global leader in automobiles and engineering.
commonConfusion: Germany's Chancellor, not the President, is the head of government and holds real executive power — the President's role is largely ceremonial.

highYieldFacts: Germany: federal parliamentary republic; Chancellor leads government; reunified 1990.
Europe's largest economy; founding EU member; automotive/engineering global leader.
India-Germany: Strategic Partnership; major EU trade/investment partner, strong in renewable energy and vocational training cooperation.
commonTraps: Confusing Germany's ceremonial President with its actual head of government, the Chancellor.
Assuming German reunification happened at the same time as the fall of the Berlin Wall — the Wall fell in 1989, formal reunification followed in 1990.
mustRemember: Germany: federal republic, EU's largest economy, reunified 1990, major India trade/tech/skills partner.
